sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Eco-tourism is often hailed as the panacea for sustainable development, promising a symbiotic relationship between conservation and economic growth. Theoretically, it incentivizes local communities to protect their natural habitats by placing a monetary value on pristine environments. However, a paradox emerges when the very influx of tourists degrades the fragile ecosystems they visit. The carbon footprint of long-haul flights, the construction of luxury lodges in buffer zones, and the inevitable disturbance to wildlife behavior patterns often outweigh the conservation benefits. True eco-tourism requires a rigorous adherence to “carrying capacity”—limiting visitor numbers to what the environment can absorb without long-term damage. Without strict regulation, “greenwashing” becomes rampant, where mass tourism masquerades as ecological sensitivity, ultimately destroying the destination’s unique value proposition.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: In the age of algorithmic feeds and 15-second video loops, the cognitive landscape of childhood is undergoing a seismic shift. Deep reading—the immersive, sustained engagement with long-form text—is increasingly being replaced by “skimming” and “scanning.” This is not merely a change in format but a rewiring of neural circuitry. Deep reading fosters empathy, critical thinking, and the ability to hold complex, contradictory ideas simultaneously. Conversely, the fragmented consumption of digital media promotes a craving for immediate dopamine hits, eroding the patience required for narrative absorption. As children lose the capacity for “cognitive patience,” we risk raising a generation that is information-rich but context-poor, capable of processing data points but struggling to weave them into meaningful tapestries of understanding.

questions.q: The primary purpose of the passage is to
opts: promote eco-tourism as the best form of travel
critique the implementation and potential downsides of eco-tourism
explain the benefits of building forest lodges
questions.why: It accepts the promise but focuses on the paradox and greenwashing. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What does the author mean by “carrying capacity”?
opts: the maximum population of a species
the limit on visitor numbers an environment can handle without damage
questions.why: Defined in the same sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, “greenwashing” involves
opts: deceptively marketing mass tourism as environmentally friendly
questions.why: Mass tourism “masquerades as ecological sensitivity”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: Why does the author describe eco-tourism as a “paradox”?
opts: It is costly but poorly equipped
The activity meant to appreciate nature often ends up damaging it
Locals dislike tourists but want their money
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What is the theoretical benefit of eco-tourism mentioned in the text?
opts: It allows hunting in restricted areas
It gives locals an economic reason to preserve nature
It removes the need for regulation
questions.why: Second sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The term “cognitive patience” implies
opts: waiting for a website to load
the mental endurance needed to engage with long, complex texts
questions.why: It is the patience “required for narrative absorption”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, deep reading is essential because
opts: it fosters empathy and critical thinking
it is the only way to learn history
questions.why: Fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.why: Last sentence; B reverses it. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The “seismic shift” refers to
opts: a fundamental change in how children process information and think
the move from books to e-readers
questions.why: “A rewiring of neural circuitry”, not just a change of format. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Select the correct preposition: “The athlete broke his own record by jumping ____ a five-feet-high bar.”
questions.why: One jumps over a bar. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Select the correct meaning of the proverb: A stitch in time saves nine
opts: nine stitches will save the damage
timely stitches will save the patient
timely action will prevent further loss
questions.why: Standard proverb. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Select the simple past tense of the verb ‘to be’: “The road ____ long and lonely.”
questions.why: Simple past of 'be' with a singular subject is 'was'. (The paper printed 'to have'; the answer key is 'was'.) GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: She said to me, “Please help me.”
opts: She requested me to help her.
She said me to help her.
She told that please help her.
She requested me to help me.
questions.why: Requests become 'requested + object + to-infinitive'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: India's first National Household Travel Survey, released in 2026, was conducted by the:
questions.why: It found 42.6% of workers mainly commute by two-wheeler. Oct 2026.

India's women's hockey team won Asian Games gold in 2026 by beating China. India last won this gold in:

questions.q: The International Day for the Eradication of Poverty is observed on:

questions.q: Goa's month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan (17 September–17 October 2026) opened with a programme called:
Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth became the first Indian woman to complete the Fighter Combat Leader course at:

questions.q: The 'Favara–UPI' corridor allows real-time remittances to India from:
The Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan, whose fifth awards were given in September 2026, ranks cities on:

questions.q: Who was appointed Chairperson of CBSE in 2026?
Who among these does NOT vote in the election of the President of India?
opts: Elected members of the Delhi assembly
Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha
Elected members of the Lok Sabha
questions.why: Article 54.

questions.q: Statement: Should defence attorneys be allowed to take part entirely by video-conference in all criminal trials? Arguments: I. Yes. It will lower the cost of legal representation and speed up disposal of cases. II. No. It compromises the right to effective legal assistance, as confidential consultation and real-time cross-examination cannot be replicated over digital links.
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.why: II rests on a fundamental right; I is a convenience. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Three years ago, the average age of a family of 5 was 24 years. Two children were born since then (one 1 year older than the other), and today the average age of the family is 20 years. What is the present age of the younger child?
questions.why: Adults now 120 + 15 = 135; family of 7 totals 140, so children sum 5: ages 2 and 3. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Deepak invests ₹1,20,000 at 12% simple interest. Kiran invests ₹1,00,000 at 10% compounded annually. Find the difference between their interest after 3 years.
questions.why: SI = 43,200. CI = 1,00,000 × (1.331 − 1) = 33,100. Difference 10,100. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following is least like the others?
questions.why: Pearl is organic (from an oyster); the rest are mined gemstones. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.why: n(n + 1): 6 × 7 = 42. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Statements: I. India's tea exports this year are the highest ever, due to demand for quality tea in Europe. II. Demand for coffee in the domestic market has risen over the last two years.
opts: Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect
Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect
Both statements are effects of independent causes
questions.why: Each statement is itself an effect (of European demand and of domestic taste), and the two are unrelated. The official key says C. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.

questions.q: If 'P × Q' means P is the mother of Q, 'P + Q' means Q is the sister of P, and 'P − Q' means P is the daughter of Q, how is 'A is the aunt of B' denoted?
questions.why: B − C: B is C's daughter; C + A: A is C's sister. So A is B's aunt. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.
Middle digit = first − last (8 − 5 = 3 …); for 751, 7 − 1 = 6, not 5. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: 396, 462, 572, 427, 671, 264
questions.why: Middle digit = sum of outer digits (3 + 6 = 9 …); 4 + 7 = 11, not 2. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.

questions.q: In a code language, 'this is not me' = 'ar rt st pt'; 'not you but him' = 'mn we rt qs'; 'me and you come' = 'yu mn pt xr'; 'but this is him' = 'ar we st qs'. What is the code for 'me'?
questions.why: 'me' is common to sentences 1 and 3; the common code is pt. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.

questions.q: In §3 Hahnemann lists among the physician's duties knowing the obstacles to recovery and how to remove them. Such obstacles are:
opts: causes that maintain the disease, such as faulty diet or living conditions
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Maintaining causes block cure.

questions.q: In chronic miasmatic diseases, Hahnemann taught that several antipsoric remedies may be needed:
opts: one after another, each given singly according to the changing symptoms
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Each prescription follows the new picture.

questions.q: By 'latent psora' Hahnemann meant:
opts: psora present in the organism without obvious outward symptoms
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. It may lie dormant until stress brings out disease.

questions.q: Profuse sweat on the head of a fat, flabby child is Calcarea carb. A child who is thin, emaciated about the neck, with a craving for salt and a map-like tongue, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Nat mur: emaciation descending from the neck, mapped tongue.

questions.q: Profuse sweat on uncovered parts, a dirty-looking skin and burning soles that are put out of the bed at night indicate:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sulphur: hot feet, burning.

questions.q: Excessive weakness, prostration and trembling in alcoholics, with vomiting of sour food and a desire for stimulants, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sulphuric acid: hurry, weakness, sour discharges.

questions.q: Wild, uncontrollable laughter alternating with weeping, inappropriate jealousy and suspicion, and a dislike of tight clothing around the neck, indicate:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Lachesis: loquacity, left side, cannot bear constriction.

questions.q: A 6C potency represents a dilution of the original substance of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Each C step is 1:100, so six steps give 10^-12.

questions.q: A prescription should be written:
opts: clearly, with the patient's name, date, remedy, potency, dose and the prescriber's signature
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Prescription rules.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's 'Doctrine of Analogy' was used to:
opts: fill in missing parts of a symptom from analogous symptoms elsewhere
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. A missing modality could be taken from another location.

questions.q: The use of a computer repertory mainly helps by:
opts: speeding up repertorisation and allowing quick comparison of remedies
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. The physician still selects and evaluates rubrics.

questions.q: The first heart sound (S1) is produced by closure of the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. S1 marks the start of ventricular systole; S2 is closure of the semilunar valves.

questions.q: The serum enzyme most specific for liver-cell injury is:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. ALT is found mainly in the liver; ALP rises in obstruction and bone disease.

questions.q: The commonest site for metastasis of carcinoma via blood is the:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Organs filtering venous blood.

questions.q: A positive Rapid Diagnostic Test for HRP-2 antigen indicates infection by:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Histidine-rich protein 2 is falciparum-specific.

questions.q: The most common type of thyroid cancer is:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. It has a good prognosis.

questions.q: Chronic eczema that is dry, scaly and worse from washing, in a patient who stands stooped and dislikes bathing, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Sulphur: aversion to bathing.

questions.q: Acute coryza with sneezing, a hot head and dry nose blocked at night but fluent by day, in a chilly, irritable patient, points to:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Nux vomica: fluent by day, blocked at night.

questions.q: The usual weight gain in a normal pregnancy is about:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Varies with pre-pregnancy BMI.

questions.q: Most children's first milk tooth erupts at about:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Lower central incisors.

questions.q: A burst abdomen after surgery in a debilitated patient is called:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Due to poor healing.

questions.q: Unilateral foul-smelling nasal discharge in a child should make one suspect:
opts: a foreign body in the nose
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Until proven otherwise.

questions.q: The 'iceberg phenomenon' of disease refers to:
opts: most cases of a disease being hidden (subclinical or undiagnosed) below the visible clinical cases
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Screening reveals the hidden part.

questions.q: Strangulation by ligature differs from hanging in that the ligature mark is usually:
opts: horizontal and encircling the neck completely, at or below the thyroid cartilage
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. In hanging the mark is oblique and high.

questions.q: Under the Consumer Protection Act, a patient may sue a doctor for:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Medical services are covered as services.
